findings.quote: Two supporting segments give MA $2$: the effort is half the load, and the free end moves twice as far as the load.
findings.problem: The effort equals half the load's weight only when the load has zero acceleration. The lesson never states this condition. Applying Newton's second law to the moving load gives 2T - mg = ma, so upward acceleration requires T greater than mg/2 even with ideal pulleys. Question 0013 explicitly tests this missing condition.
findings.source: [OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Section 6.1: equilibrium and Newton's second law](https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/6-1-solving-problems-with-newtons-laws)
